module MPY-METHODS
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports K-EQUAL
  imports MPY-STR
  imports MPY-LIST

  // method-call routing + arg-eval live in call.k; this module owns applyMethod.
  syntax Val ::= applyMethod(Val, String, Vals) [function]

  // ==== string predicates (Python semantics) =================================
  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "isupper", .Vals) => hasUpper(CS) andBool notBool hasLower(CS)
  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "islower", .Vals) => hasLower(CS) andBool notBool hasUpper(CS)
  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "isalpha", .Vals) => notBool (CS ==K .IntSeq) andBool allAlpha(CS)
  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "isdigit", .Vals) => notBool (CS ==K .IntSeq) andBool allDigit(CS)

  // ==== case maps ============================================================
  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "lower",    .Vals) => str(mapLower(CS))
  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "upper",    .Vals) => str(mapUpper(CS))
  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "swapcase", .Vals) => str(mapSwap(CS))

  syntax IntSeq ::= joinCodes(IntSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
  rule joinCodes(_:IntSeq, .ValSeq) => .IntSeq
  rule joinCodes(_:IntSeq, vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), .ValSeq)) => CS
  rule joinCodes(SEP:IntSeq, vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)))
    => seqConcat(CS, seqConcat(SEP, joinCodes(SEP, vCons(V, R))))

  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "count", str(PC:IntSeq), .Vals) => cntSub(CS, PC)
  syntax Int ::= cntSub(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function]
  rule cntSub(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq) => 0
  rule cntSub(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), PC:IntSeq) => 1 +Int cntSub(dropIS(iCons(C, R), isLen(PC)), PC)
       requires strPrefix(PC, iCons(C, R)) andBool isLen(PC) >Int 0
  rule cntSub(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), PC:IntSeq) => cntSub(R, PC)
       requires notBool strPrefix(PC, iCons(C, R)) orBool isLen(PC) <=Int 0
  syntax IntSeq ::= dropIS(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
  rule dropIS(S:IntSeq, N:Int) => S requires N <=Int 0
  rule dropIS(.IntSeq, _:Int) => .IntSeq [owise]
  rule dropIS(iCons(_:Int, R:IntSeq), N:Int) => dropIS(R, N -Int 1) requires N >Int 0

  syntax IntSeq ::= trimWS(IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule trimWS(.IntSeq) => .IntSeq
  rule trimWS(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => trimWS(R) requires isWSC(C)
  rule trimWS(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => iCons(C, R) requires notBool isWSC(C)

  rule splitSep(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), SEP:Int, CUR:IntSeq) => vCons(str(CUR), splitSep(R, SEP, .IntSeq))

  syntax IntSeq ::= replaceC(IntSeq, Int, Int) [function, total]

  rule replaceC(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int, B:Int) => iCons(B, replaceC(R, A, B)) requires C ==Int A

  rule swapC(C:Int) => C         [owise]

  syntax IntSeq ::= mapLower(IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule mapLower(.IntSeq) => .IntSeq
  rule mapLower(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => iCons(lowerC(C), mapLower(S))

  syntax IntSeq ::= mapUpper(IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule mapUpper(.IntSeq) => .IntSeq
  rule mapUpper(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => iCons(upperC(C), mapUpper(S))

  syntax IntSeq ::= mapSwap(IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule mapSwap(.IntSeq) => .IntSeq
  rule mapSwap(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => iCons(swapC(C), mapSwap(S))

  syntax Bool ::= startsWith(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule startsWith(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)               => true
  rule startsWith(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
  rule startsWith(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => A ==Int B andBool startsWith(As, Bs)
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/float.k — MPY-FLOAT
//
// Minimal, TRUSTED float support. K/Haskell (kprove) has no usable symbolic IEEE-754 theory and
// no Int2Float hook, so a float value stays an OPAQUE proof-domain primitive: `intFloatDiv(I, F)`
// (the Python true division I / F) is `[no-evaluators]` for kprove — it never reduces on symbolic
// input, and the proof verifies only the STRUCTURE (the result is the exact term the program
// builds). The `[concrete]` rule evaluates it for krun (llvm HAS the Int2Float / /Float hooks), so
// smoke tests run the real float value.
//
// Only the pieces needed so far: Float as a Val, the float literal, and Int / float true division
// (the `a * h / 2.0` idiom). More float ops (float +/-/*, comparison) are added as float problems
// need them — kept minimal + sound.

module MPY-FLOAT
  imports MPY-OPERATORS
  imports MPY-BUILTINS
  imports FLOAT

  // Float is a value; the float literal evaluates to the K Float.
  syntax Val ::= Float
  rule <k> Float(F:Float) => F ... </k>

  // Int / float true division. OPAQUE for kprove (no-evaluators); concrete for krun.
  syntax Float ::= intFloatDiv(Int, Float) [function, total, symbol(intFloatDiv), no-evaluators]
  rule intFloatDiv(I:Int, F:Float) => Int2Float(I, 53, 11) /Float F [concrete]

  rule applyBin("/", I:Int, F:Float) => intFloatDiv(I, F)

  // Int / Int true division (Python: always a float). OPAQUE for kprove; concrete for krun.
  syntax Float ::= divII(Int, Int) [function, total, symbol(divII), no-evaluators]
  rule divII(I1:Int, I2:Int) => Int2Float(I1, 53, 11) /Float Int2Float(I2, 53, 11) [concrete]
  rule applyBin("/", I1:Int, I2:Int) => divII(I1, I2)

  // float % float (e.g. `number % 1.0` = the fractional part). OPAQUE for kprove, concrete for
  // krun. Python's float `%` is floor-based: a % b = a - floor(a/b)*b (K's %Float is IEEE
  // remainder, which differs — 3.5 %Float 1.0 = -0.5 vs Python 0.5 — so it is NOT used).
  syntax Float ::= floatMod(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(floatMod), no-evaluators]
  rule floatMod(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 -Float (floorFloat(F1 /Float F2) *Float F2) [concrete]
  rule applyBin("%", F1:Float, F2:Float) => floatMod(F1, F2)

  // float equality — for concrete krun asserts (e.g. `area == 7.5`); the FLOAT.eq hook is fine on
  // concrete floats. kprove proofs return floats structurally and do not compare them.
  rule applyCmp("==", F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 ==Float F2
  rule applyCmp("!=", F1:Float, F2:Float) => notBool (F1 ==Float F2)

  // float `<` and abs — OPAQUE for kprove ([no-evaluators], so a SYMBOLIC float compare stays an
  // uninterpreted Bool a proof case-splits on — a SINGLE compare per branch, not a nonlinear cascade),
  // [concrete] for krun. Additive, sort-disjoint from the Int rules. (has_close_elements: the pairwise
  // `abs(a-b) < t` proximity test.)
  syntax Bool ::= floatLt(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(floatLt), no-evaluators]
  rule floatLt(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 <Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyCmp("<", F1:Float, F2:Float) => floatLt(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= absF(Float) [function, total, symbol(absF), no-evaluators]
  rule absF(F:Float) => absFloat(F) [concrete]
  rule applyBuiltin("abs", F:Float, .Vals) => absF(F)

  // ==== math.ceil ===========================================================
  // `import X` is a no-op (we intercept the specific math functions syntactically; `math` itself is
  // never bound as a value).
  rule <k> Import(_:String) => .K ... </k>

  // math.ceil(x): ceiling to an int. Intercepted at the Call BEFORE `math` is looked up (higher
  // priority than the generic Attribute/method dispatch in call.k).
  syntax KItem ::= "#mathCeil"
  rule <k> Call(Attribute(Name("math"), "ceil"), (E:Expr, .Exprs)) => E ~> #mathCeil ... </k> [priority(40)]
  rule <k> V:Val ~> #mathCeil => ceilF(V) ... </k>

  // math.floor(x) — same interception shape as math.ceil
  syntax KItem ::= "#mathFloor"
  rule <k> Call(Attribute(Name("math"), "floor"), (E:Expr, .Exprs)) => E ~> #mathFloor ... </k> [priority(40)]
  rule <k> V:Val ~> #mathFloor => floorFI(V) ... </k>
  syntax Int ::= floorFI(Val) [function, total, symbol(floorFI)]
  rule floorFI(I:Int)   => I                        [concrete]
  rule floorFI(F:Float) => Float2Int(floorFloat(F)) [concrete]

  // bare floor/ceil (bound by `from math import floor, ceil`)
  rule applyBuiltin("floor", V:Val, .Vals) => floorFI(V)
  rule applyBuiltin("ceil",  V:Val, .Vals) => ceilF(V)

  // math.pow(x, y) — a two-arg interception onto powF (ints promote)
  syntax KItem ::= #mathPow1(Expr) | #mathPow2(Val)
  rule <k> Call(Attribute(Name("math"), "pow"), (E1:Expr, E2:Expr, .Exprs)) => E1 ~> #mathPow1(E2) ... </k> [priority(40)]
  rule <k> V1:Val ~> #mathPow1(E2:Expr) => E2 ~> #mathPow2(V1) ... </k>
  rule <k> V2:Val ~> #mathPow2(V1:Val) => powF(toF(V1), toF(V2)) ... </k>
  syntax Float ::= toF(Val) [function, total, symbol(toF)]
  rule toF(F:Float) => F        [concrete]
  rule toF(I:Int)   => intToF(I) [concrete]

  // ceilF: math.ceil as an Int. TOTAL (K trusts it; a symbolic list element stays opaque for
  // kprove — structural). [concrete] so the Int2Float/ceilFloat hooks only run for krun (llvm).
  // Matches Python incl. negatives: ceil(-2.4) = -2 = Float2Int(ceilFloat(-2.4)).
  syntax Int ::= ceilF(Val) [function, total, symbol(ceilF)]
  rule ceilF(I:Int)   => I                       [concrete]
  rule ceilF(F:Float) => Float2Int(ceilFloat(F)) [concrete]

  // unary minus on a float (e.g. the literal -2.4 = UnaryOp("-", Float(2.4))). Concrete for krun;
  // proofs use symbolic elements, never a float literal.
  rule applyUn("-", F:Float) => 0.0 -Float F

  // ---- float - / / / + (OPAQUE for kprove [no-evaluators], concrete for krun) — for float-list
  // element maps (x - lo) / (hi - lo). Mirror intFloatDiv: additive, sort-disjoint from the Int rules.
  syntax Float ::= subF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(subF), no-evaluators]
  rule subF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 -Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("-", F1:Float, F2:Float) => subF(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= divF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(divF), no-evaluators]
  rule divF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 /Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("/", F1:Float, F2:Float) => divF(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= addF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(addF), no-evaluators]
  rule addF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 +Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("+", F1:Float, F2:Float) => addF(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= mulF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(mulF), no-evaluators]
  rule mulF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 *Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("*", F1:Float, F2:Float) => mulF(F1, F2)

  syntax Float ::= powF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(powF), no-evaluators]
  rule powF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 ^Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyBin("**", F1:Float, F2:Float) => powF(F1, F2)

  // ---- the remaining comparisons (gtF promoted from find_zero — its summaries
  //      case-split on the atom; >= / <= derive from the two opaque compares) ----
  syntax Bool ::= gtF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(gtF), no-evaluators]
  rule gtF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 >Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyCmp(">",  F1:Float, F2:Float) => gtF(F1, F2)
  rule applyCmp(">=", F1:Float, F2:Float) => notBool floatLt(F1, F2)
  rule applyCmp("<=", F1:Float, F2:Float) => notBool gtF(F1, F2)

  // ---- mixed Int/Float operators promote the Int side (n ** 0.5 etc.) ----
  rule applyBin("**", I:Int, F:Float) => powF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("**", F:Float, I:Int) => powF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("-",  I:Int, F:Float) => subF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("-",  F:Float, I:Int) => subF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("+",  I:Int, F:Float) => addF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("+",  F:Float, I:Int) => addF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("*",  I:Int, F:Float) => mulF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("*",  F:Float, I:Int) => mulF(F, intToF(I))

  // ---- mixed Int == Float (shared eqF; opaque symbolic / concrete twin) ----
  syntax Bool ::= eqF(Float, Float) [function, total, symbol(eqF), no-evaluators]
  rule eqF(F1:Float, F2:Float) => F1 ==Float F2 [concrete]
  rule applyCmp("==", I:Int, F:Float) => eqF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp("==", F:Float, I:Int) => eqF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp("!=", I:Int, F:Float) => notBool eqF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp("!=", F:Float, I:Int) => notBool eqF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp("<",  I:Int, F:Float) => floatLt(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp("<",  F:Float, I:Int) => floatLt(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp(">",  I:Int, F:Float) => gtF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp(">",  F:Float, I:Int) => gtF(F, intToF(I))

  // ---- x == None (promoted from 137; `is` cases live in operators.k) ----
  rule applyCmp("==", V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
  rule applyCmp("!=", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)

  // ---- float(str): decimal parse (promoted from 137's defined chain) ----
  // digits '.' digits, optional leading '-'; concrete evaluation only (the
  // symbolic side stays an opaque decStrToF term a proof case-splits on).
  syntax Float ::= decStrToF(IntSeq) [function, total, symbol(decStrToF), no-evaluators]
  rule decStrToF(iCons(45, CS:IntSeq)) => 0.0 -Float decStrToF(CS) [concrete]
  rule decStrToF(CS:IntSeq)
    => intToF(intPart(CS)) +Float (intToF(fracPart(CS)) /Float intToF(fracScale(CS)))
       requires isLen(CS) >Int 0 andBool headIS(CS) =/=Int 45 [concrete]
  syntax Int ::= headIS(IntSeq) [function]
  rule headIS(iCons(C:Int, _:IntSeq)) => C
  syntax Int ::= intPart(IntSeq) [function, total] | intPartAcc(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
  rule intPart(CS:IntSeq) => intPartAcc(CS, 0)
  rule intPartAcc(.IntSeq, A:Int) => A
  rule intPartAcc(iCons(46, _:IntSeq), A:Int) => A
  rule intPartAcc(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int) => intPartAcc(R, A *Int 10 +Int (C -Int 48))
       requires C =/=Int 46
  syntax Int ::= fracPart(IntSeq) [function, total] | fracAcc(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
  rule fracPart(.IntSeq) => 0
  rule fracPart(iCons(46, R:IntSeq)) => fracAcc(R, 0)
  rule fracPart(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => fracPart(R) requires C =/=Int 46
  rule fracAcc(.IntSeq, A:Int) => A
  rule fracAcc(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int) => fracAcc(R, A *Int 10 +Int (C -Int 48))
  syntax Int ::= fracScale(IntSeq) [function, total] | fscAcc(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
  rule fracScale(.IntSeq) => 1
  rule fracScale(iCons(46, R:IntSeq)) => fscAcc(R, 1)
  rule fracScale(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => fracScale(R) requires C =/=Int 46
  rule fscAcc(.IntSeq, A:Int) => A
  rule fscAcc(iCons(_:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int) => fscAcc(R, A *Int 10)
  rule applyBuiltin("float", str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals) => decStrToF(CS)
  rule applyBuiltin("float", I:Int, .Vals)          => intToF(I)
  rule applyBuiltin("float", F:Float, .Vals)        => F

  // ---- float / int division (promoted from mean_absolute_deviation) ----
  syntax Float ::= divFloatIntV(Float, Int) [function, total, symbol(divFloatIntV), no-evaluators]
  rule divFloatIntV(F:Float, I:Int) => F /Float Int2Float(I, 53, 11) [concrete]
  rule applyBin("/", F:Float, I:Int) => divFloatIntV(F, I)

  // ---- int -> float promotion for the remaining mixed arithmetic/compares ----
  syntax Float ::= intToF(Int) [function, total, symbol(intToF), no-evaluators]
  rule intToF(I:Int) => Int2Float(I, 53, 11) [concrete]
  rule applyBin("+", I:Int, F:Float) => addF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("+", F:Float, I:Int) => addF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("-", I:Int, F:Float) => subF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("-", F:Float, I:Int) => subF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyBin("*", I:Int, F:Float) => mulF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyBin("*", F:Float, I:Int) => mulF(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp("<", I:Int, F:Float) => floatLt(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp("<", F:Float, I:Int) => floatLt(F, intToF(I))
  rule applyCmp(">", I:Int, F:Float) => gtF(intToF(I), F)
  rule applyCmp(">", F:Float, I:Int) => gtF(F, intToF(I))

  // ---- conversions: int(float) truncates toward zero; float(int); round; math.sqrt ----
  syntax Int ::= truncF(Float) [function, total, symbol(truncF), no-evaluators]
  rule truncF(F:Float) => #if F >=Float 0.0 #then Float2Int(floorFloat(F)) #else Float2Int(ceilFloat(F)) #fi [concrete]
  rule applyBuiltin("int", F:Float, .Vals) => truncF(F)

  rule applyBuiltin("float", I:Int, .Vals)   => intToF(I)
  rule applyBuiltin("float", F:Float, .Vals) => F

  // round: Python half-even (banker's); round(F, N) scales by 10^N
  syntax Int ::= roundF(Float) [function, total, symbol(roundF), no-evaluators]
  rule roundF(F:Float)
    => #if (F -Float floorFloat(F)) ==Float 0.5
       #then (#if Float2Int(floorFloat(F)) %Int 2 ==Int 0
              #then Float2Int(floorFloat(F)) #else Float2Int(ceilFloat(F)) #fi)
       #else Float2Int(floorFloat(F +Float 0.5)) #fi [concrete]
  syntax Float ::= roundFN(Float, Int) [function, total, symbol(roundFN), no-evaluators]
  rule roundFN(F:Float, N:Int)
    => Int2Float(roundF(F *Float Int2Float(10 ^Int N, 53, 11)), 53, 11)
       /Float Int2Float(10 ^Int N, 53, 11) [concrete]
  rule applyBuiltin("round", F:Float, .Vals)        => roundF(F)
  rule applyBuiltin("round", F:Float, N:Int, .Vals) => roundFN(F, N)

  syntax Float ::= sqrtF(Float) [function, total, symbol(sqrtF), no-evaluators]
  rule sqrtF(F:Float) => sqrtFloat(F) [concrete]
  syntax KItem ::= "#mathSqrt"
  rule <k> Call(Attribute(Name("math"), "sqrt"), (E:Expr, .Exprs)) => E ~> #mathSqrt ... </k> [priority(40)]
  rule <k> F:Float ~> #mathSqrt => sqrtF(F) ... </k>
  rule <k> I:Int ~> #mathSqrt => sqrtF(intToF(I)) ... </k>

  // ---- min / max over a FLOAT list — FLOAT branch of the shared #minCont0/#maxCont0 folds (which
  // seed/step with `requires isInt(V)`, so they are STUCK on floats). These add the `requires
  // isFloat(V)` seed + a Float-accumulator fold via K's minFloat/maxFloat — concrete for krun. A proof
  // over a SYMBOLIC float list intercepts min/max problem-locally to an opaque minVF/maxVF (at
  // #applyK, priority 40, in its verification.k) BEFORE #minAcc0, so this fold is krun-only. Additive:
  // the isFloat guard is disjoint from the existing isInt one.
  syntax KItem ::= #maxAccF(Iterable, Float) | #maxContF(Float)
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont0 => #maxAccF(R, {V}:>Float) ... </k> requires isFloat(V)
  rule <k> #maxAccF(IT:Iterable, M:Float) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxContF(M) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #maxContF(M:Float) => M ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxContF(M:Float) => #maxAccF(R, maxFloat(M, {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
       requires isFloat(V)

  syntax KItem ::= #minAccF(Iterable, Float) | #minContF(Float)
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont0 => #minAccF(R, {V}:>Float) ... </k> requires isFloat(V)
  rule <k> #minAccF(IT:Iterable, M:Float) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minContF(M) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #minContF(M:Float) => M ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minContF(M:Float) => #minAccF(R, minFloat(M, {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
       requires isFloat(V)

  // ---- sum over a float list (krun; mirrors the min/max float paths). The Int-only shared
  // #sumCont sticks on a Float yield; switch to a Float-headed fold via addF (concrete twin).
  // The switch guard carries the SYNTACTIC negation of the Int rule's guard so a symbolic proof
  // with isInt(V) in its path condition refutes this branch without sort reasoning.
  syntax KItem ::= #sumAccF(Iterable, Float) | #sumContF(Float)
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumCont(ACC:Int)
        => #sumAccF(R, addF(intToF(ACC), {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
       requires isFloat(V) andBool notBool (isInt(V) orBool isBool(V))
  rule <k> #sumAccF(IT:Iterable, ACC:Float) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #sumContF(ACC) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #sumContF(ACC:Float) => ACC ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumContF(ACC:Float)
        => #sumAccF(R, addF(ACC, {V}:>Float)) ... </k>
       requires isFloat(V)
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumContF(ACC:Float)
        => #sumAccF(R, addF(ACC, intToF(intOf(V)))) ... </k>
       requires isInt(V) orBool isBool(V)
endmodule

        case["contract_valid"] = valid(case["operators"], case["operands"])

        case["implementations_match"] = case["canonical_result"] == case["candidate_result"]
        failures += int(not case["contract_valid"] or not case["implementations_match"])
    output = {
        "spec_operator_shapes_from_static_inspection": [
            ["+"],
            ["-"],
            ["*"],
            ["//"],
            ["**"],
            ["-", "-"],
            ["//", "//"],
            ["**", "**"],
            ["+", "*", "-"],
            ["+", "*", "**", "//", "-"],

*** Add File: /audit-output/REVIEW.md
+# Independent adversarial audit — 160-do-algebra
+
+Generation condition: `semantics`  
+Rendered semantics mode: `SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`
+
+## Executive decision
+
+The reconstructed K claims are real, non-vacuous partial-correctness theorems
+about the submitted `solution.mpy`: all ten close independently, the launcher
+loads the exact submitted AST, and no candidate-local rule replaces
+`_evaluate` with an oracle or a task-answer shortcut.
+
+They are not, however, a proof of `do_algebra` on the prompt's intended input
+domain. `spec.k` enumerates ten fixed operator-list shapes, with several
+fixed operands, and contains no entry claim quantified over an arbitrary
+contract-valid operator/operand list. Contract-valid examples such as two
+additions, an exponentiation other than `2 ** 5`, most mixed expressions, and
+all sufficiently long expressions satisfy no claim. That is a material
+adequacy failure, not merely thin supporting evidence. The candidate therefore
+does not contain the requested whole-program partial-correctness proof.
+
+All candidate files were treated as untrusted. Candidate compiled artifacts,
+caches, scripts, and claimed outputs were not used as proof evidence.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+
+### Infrastructure and semantics-mode boundary
+
+The trusted mount is consistent with `SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`:
+`/reference/reference-semantics` exists. No infrastructure breach was found,
+so a candidate verdict is appropriate.
+
+The candidate's `reference-semantics/` is recursively identical to the trusted
+tree:
+
+- `diff -ru --no-dereference /reference/reference-semantics
+  /candidate/reference-semantics` exited 0.
+- The candidate semantics tree contains no symlink.
+- No file is missing from, added to, mistyped in, or changed relative to the
+  trusted semantics tree.
+
+The candidate `prompt.py` and `py2mpy.py` are also byte-identical to their
+trusted counterparts; both diffs exited 0 and the hashes agree. The complete
+type manifest, commands, statuses, and hashes are in
+[01_integrity.log](evidence/01_integrity.log), generated by
+[01_integrity.sh](evidence/01_integrity.sh).
+
+### Missing provenance artifacts
+
+The following requested generation artifacts are absent from `/candidate`:
+
+- `run-input.json`
+- `metrics.json`
+- `codex-last.txt`
+- `codex-output.log`
+- any structured generation trace (the explicit
+  `generation-trace.json` check failed, and no trace/log/JSON alternative was
+  present)
+
+The executable source artifacts `solution.py`, `solution.mpy`, `spec.k`,
+`verification.k`, `prompt.py`, `py2mpy.py`, and the supplied-semantics directory
+are regular files/directories, not symlinks. The candidate also contains
+untrusted extras (`prove.sh`, `smoke.mpy`, `kore-exec.tar.gz`, and a Python
+`__pycache__`); they were ignored for reconstruction. The missing provenance
+logs reduce auditability, but they do not create an infrastructure error and
+do not substitute for the independent checks below.
+
+## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks
+
+### Natural-language contract
+
+From trusted `/reference/prompt.py` and `/reference/canonical.py`, `do_algebra`
+takes:
+
+- at least one operator from `+`, `-`, `*`, `//`, `**`;
+- at least two non-negative integer operands;
+- exactly one more operand than operator;
+- and returns the Python evaluation of the interleaved expression, including
+  Python precedence, left associativity for `+`, `-`, `*`, `//`, and right
+  associativity for `**`.
+
+The prompt does not exclude a zero divisor. The canonical implementation raises
+`ZeroDivisionError` for such an expression instead of returning an integer.
+Accordingly, a normal-return theorem must either model that exceptional path or
+state a sufficient nonzero-divisor precondition.
+
+### Source algorithm
+
+`solution.py` implements a precedence parser by recursive interval evaluation:
+
+- level 0 scans from right to left for `+`/`-`, producing left associativity;
+- level 1 scans from right to left for `*`/`//`;
+- level 2 scans from left to right for `**`, producing right associativity;
+- level 3 returns the selected operand.
+
+This is a different algorithm from the canonical string construction plus
+`eval`, which is acceptable if behavior agrees.
+
+### Translator fidelity
+
+Fresh translation with the trusted translator:
+
+```text
+python3 /reference/py2mpy.py /candidate/solution.py
+```
+
+exited 0. The result is byte-identical to `/candidate/solution.mpy`; both have
+SHA-256
+`4e1c9df6f7e7d5229be2910bf7215954e8c7789d9603370de5ca7c5b1c2306d4`.
+See [02_fidelity.log](evidence/02_fidelity.log).
+
+### Independent differential execution
+
+[02_differential.py](evidence/02_differential.py) independently imports the
+trusted canonical entry point and candidate entry point. It runs:
+
+- the prompt example;
+- minimum two-operand cases for all five operators;
+- zero operands and `0 ** 0`;
+- division by zero, comparing exception type and message;
+- both scan directions and all associativity/precedence boundaries;
+- the all-precedence expression;
+- 400 deterministic generated cases using lengths 1 through 5, all operator
+  tokens, and operands 0 through 8. Generated cases contain at most one
+  exponentiation to bound arithmetic size; adjacent exponentiation is covered
+  separately.
+
+The exact command exited 0 with:
+
+```text
+{"case_count": 418, "mismatch_count": 0, "seed": 160}
+```
+
+See [02_differential.log](evidence/02_differential.log) and the complete
+[02_differential-results.json](evidence/02_differential-results.json). This is
+strong finite fidelity evidence, not a universal equivalence proof.
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+All required sources were copied to `/tmp/audit-work/rebuild`. No candidate
+compiled definition, cache, `kore-exec.tar.gz`, or prior proof result was
+copied. The initial scratch scan found no `*-kompiled` directory.
+
+The live toolchain was K version `v7.1.337` (build date 2026-06-18).
+
+### Concrete and proof definitions
+
+The following independent reconstruction succeeded:
+
+```text
+kompile reference-semantics/semantics.k --backend llvm \
+  --main-module MPY-KRUN --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
+  --output-definition runtime-audit-kompiled
+
+krun concrete-tests.mpy --definition runtime-audit-kompiled --output none
+
+kompile verification.k --backend haskell \
+  --main-module VERIFICATION --syntax-module VERIFICATION \
+  --output-definition verification-audit-kompiled
+```
+
+Both `kompile` commands and `krun` exited 0. The reviewer-generated concrete
+program contains ten assertions covering the prompt example, every primitive
+operator, zero/negative results, associativity, and mixed precedence. Its
+generator is [03_make_concrete_tests.py](evidence/03_make_concrete_tests.py).
+Exact commands and bounded build output are in
+[03_rebuild.log](evidence/03_rebuild.log).
+
+The compiler emitted supplied-semantics warnings about several non-exhaustive
+`total` functions, including `valSeqAt`. No candidate-local warning identifies
+an execution shortcut. Relevant totality is assessed in Stage 5.
+
+### Exact program pinning
+
+Fresh `kast --expand-macros` output for parsed `solution.mpy` was compared with
+fresh expansion of `solutionProgram`. `cmp` exited 0; both KORE files have
+SHA-256
+`6aa2b0dd7beba2ebea185c24c803aada04907e1f1bc9666ac3f12cd26b0a3040`.
+Thus the proof macro denotes exactly the submitted translated program.
+
+### Every positive claim
+
+Each label was run separately with:
+
+```text
+kprove spec.k --definition verification-audit-kompiled \
+  --spec-module SPEC --claims <label>
+```
+
+Every run exited 0 and contained an exact `#Top` line:
+
+| Label | Exit | Exact `#Top` |
+|---|---:|---|
+| `plus` | 0 | yes |
+| `minus` | 0 | yes |
+| `times` | 0 | yes |
+| `floor` | 0 | yes |
+| `power` | 0 | yes |
+| `minus-assoc` | 0 | yes |
+| `floor-assoc` | 0 | yes |
+| `power-assoc` | 0 | yes |
+| `prompt-precedence` | 0 | yes |
+| `mixed-precedence` | 0 | yes |
+
+The aggregate command/status record is
+[03_positive_claims.log](evidence/03_positive_claims.log); separate bounded raw
+logs are preserved as `evidence/03_claim_<label>.log`.
+
+Clean reconstruction therefore passes for the theorems the candidate actually
+states.
+
+## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning
+
+### Entry claims in plain language
+
+Every claim starts in the normal module configuration: environment 0, empty
+module scope with the trusted builtins parent, empty heap and call stack,
+`noRet`, `NoExc`, and exit code 0. Every claim requires those observable cells
+to return to the same values; only the final scope map is existentially
+abstracted. The `<k>` result is an explicit expression, not a fresh variable.
+
+| Label | Input/precondition | Required result |
+|---|---|---|
+| `plus` | exactly `["+"], [A,B]`; `A,B >= 0` | `A+B` |
+| `minus` | exactly `["-"], [A,B]`; `A,B >= 0` | `A-B` |
+| `times` | exactly `["*"], [A,B]`; `A,B >= 0` | `A*B` |
+| `floor` | exactly `["//"], [A,B]`; `A >= 0`, `B > 0` | Python floor quotient of `A/B` |
+| `power` | exactly `["**"], [2,5]` | `32` |
+| `minus-assoc` | exactly `["-","-"], [A,B,C]`; all non-negative | `(A-B)-C` |
+| `floor-assoc` | exactly `["//","//"], [20,3,2]` | `3` |
+| `power-assoc` | exactly `["**","**"], [2,3,2]` | `512` |
+| `prompt-precedence` | exactly `["+","*","-"], [A,B,C,D]`; all non-negative | `(A+B*C)-D` |
+| `mixed-precedence` | exactly `["+","*","**","//","-"], [A,B,2,3,E,F]`; `A,B,F >= 0`, `E > 0` | `A + floor(B*8/E) - F` |
+
+No helper or loop claims exist. Symbolic execution runs each real `_evaluate`
+body and each bounded loop under the supplied semantics. `runDoAlgebra` only
+loads the exact program and performs an ordinary call. It does not bypass,
+return from, or summarize the program.
+
+### Satisfiable witnesses
+
+A ground state satisfying every entry precondition was exhibited. All ten
+claimed results agree with both Python implementations; examples include
+`A=2,B=3` for the three binary arithmetic claims, `A=7,B=3` for floor
+division, `20,5,3` for subtraction associativity, and `A=4,B=3,E=5,F=1` for
+the mixed claim. The complete ledger is
+[04_claim_witnesses.json](evidence/04_claim_witnesses.json); its checker exited
+0 with ten witnesses and zero failures.
+
+### Material coverage failure
+
+These ten claims do not quantify over arbitrary operator sequences. Static
+inspection gives only the ten exact shapes listed above. For example, all of
+the following satisfy the prompt contract, execute normally, and agree in the
+two Python implementations, but match no claim:
+
+| Operators | Operands | Result | Why unclaimed |
+|---|---|---:|---|
+| `["+","+"]` | `[1,2,3]` | 6 | no two-addition claim |
+| `["**"]` | `[3,4]` | 81 | the only one-power claim fixes `2,5` |
+| `["+","-","*","//"]` | `[10,2,3,4,2]` | 6 | operator shape absent |
+| `["+","*","-","+","//","*"]` | `[2,3,4,5,6,2,7]` | 30 | every claim has at most five operators |
+
+See [04_uncovered_cases.log](evidence/04_uncovered_cases.log) and
+[04_uncovered_cases.json](evidence/04_uncovered_cases.json). There are
+infinitely many such unclaimed inputs. The successful theorems cannot be
+composed into a general result because there is no induction, arbitrary
+`ValSeq` entry claim, recursive evaluator theorem, or exhaustive operator-list
+decomposition.
+
+Real-program pinning and result constraint pass for the ten stated claims.
+Adequacy for the requested program contract fails.
+
+## 5. Rule-by-rule static soundness review
+
+### Exhaustive inventory
+
+[05_rule_inventory.txt](evidence/05_rule_inventory.txt) and
+[05_rule_inventory.json](evidence/05_rule_inventory.json) preserve the exact
+line, module, complete declaration/rule text, attributes, and classification
+for every entry in:
+
+- supplied `reference-semantics/semantics.k`;
+- all 23 supplied helper K files;
+- candidate `verification.k`;
+- candidate `spec.k`.
+
+Inventory totals:
+
+| Item | Count |
+|---|---:|
+| Sources | 26 |
+| Syntax declarations | 231 |
+| Ordinary/macro semantic rules | 703 |
+| Function declarations | 146 |
+| `total` declarations | 108 |
+| `functional` declarations | 0 |
+| Opaque (`no-evaluators`) declarations | 22 |
+| Priority rules | 45 |
+| Simplification rules | 0 |
+| Reachability claims | 10 |
+
+The per-source decision applying to every inventoried rule is recorded in
+[05_rule_assessment.md](evidence/05_rule_assessment.md). The exact mapping from
+each submitted-program construct to syntax and operational rules is
+[05_used_construct_map.md](evidence/05_used_construct_map.md).
+
+### Reachable supplied-semantics slice
+
+The submitted program uses `Module`, `FuncDef`, `Params`, `Name`, `Int`, `Str`,
+`Assign`, `AugAssign`, `If`, `While`, `Compare`/`CmpOp`, `BinOp`, `Subscript`,
+`Call`, `Return`, expression/statement sequences, and the `len` builtin. Each
+has both a declaration and a reachable rule path:
+
+- module loading and statement sequencing execute both real function bodies;
+- lexical lookup selects `_evaluate`, `do_algebra`, locals, and trusted `len`
+  through the actual environment chain;
+- `seqstrict`/strict attributes and explicit contexts enforce operand,
+  condition, callee, and left-to-right argument evaluation;
+- function call rules bind parameters, push the complete continuation and
+  caller environment, and return/pop without discarding unrelated control;
+- the while rules reevaluate the real guard and body;
+- subscripting the bare read-only claim lists uses structural in-bounds access;
+- integer/string dispatch implements exactly the comparisons and arithmetic
+  used by `_evaluate`;
+- scope allocation is LIFO and is restored; the program performs no heap
+  allocation or mutation on the bare read-only input values.
+
+The claim-visible configuration is preserved: final environment, scope
+location, heap, heap location, stack, return state, exception state, and exit
+code are constrained. Only the internal final scope contents are
+existentially framed.
+
+The 22 supplied opaque symbols consist of 19 float operations, `sortVS`,
+`sortKeyVS`, and `md5hexCodes`. None is syntactically reachable from this
+integer/list/string program. They influence no branch, return, state,
+exception, or postcondition in any claim.
+
+The supplied semantics is ASCII-limited for strings, but all operator tokens
+are ASCII. Bare list values differ from ordinary allocated Python list objects,
+but the program only reads them, so identity/allocation differences are
+unobservable here. Division-by-zero exception semantics is not exercised by
+any positive floor-division claim because each divisor is fixed positive or
+guarded positive.
+
+### Candidate-local rule decisions
+
+`verification.k` adds eight rules:
+
+1. `solutionProgram` is a macro definition. Fresh macro expansion is identical
+   to parsed `solution.mpy`; it does not replace execution.
+2. Five operator-token macros map to the exact ASCII code sequences for `+`,
+   `-`, `*`, `//`, and `**`. They are disjoint and mathematically exact.
+3. `floorQuot(A,B) = (A - pyMod(A,B))/B` is a definitional postcondition
+   helper. It does not replace program execution and is correct for every
+   positive divisor used by a claim.
+4. `runDoAlgebra` is a launcher that schedules
+   `#loadAll(solutionProgram)` followed by an ordinary `do_algebra` call.
+
+There is no candidate-local opaque symbol, priority rule, simplification rule,
+auxiliary claim, circularity, return bridge, or oracle. No task answer is
+encoded into execution semantics.
+
+One narrow declaration defect remains: `floorQuot` is marked unguarded
+`[function, total]`, including `B=0`, while its RHS contains undefined modulo
+and division by zero. All actual uses have positive divisors. I found no false
+conclusion witness enabled on a claim path, so I do not label this rule
+unsound; it is an over-broad totality/evidence gap that should be repaired with
+a nonzero guard or narrowed sort/domain.
+
+No inventoried rule is claimed here to enable a false result on an intended
+claim input, so there is no unsupported unsoundness accusation requiring a
+false-conclusion witness. The final rejection instead rests on the explicit
+coverage witness in Stage 4.
+
+## 6. Fresh non-vacuity test
+
+No candidate `spec-vacuity.k` was present. I created a fresh mutation,
+[06_spec-vacuity.k](evidence/06_spec-vacuity.k), changing the `plus` result from
+`A+B` to the false result `A+B+1`. `A=0,B=0` is a concrete satisfying witness.
+
+The mutation was copied into scratch and run against the freshly rebuilt
+definition:
+
+```text
+kprove spec-vacuity.k --definition verification-audit-kompiled \
+  --spec-module SPEC-VACUITY --dry-run

# Independent adversarial audit — 160-do-algebra

Generation condition: `semantics`  
Rendered semantics mode: `SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`

## Executive decision

The reconstructed K claims are real, non-vacuous partial-correctness theorems
about the submitted `solution.mpy`: all ten close independently, the launcher
loads the exact submitted AST, and no candidate-local rule replaces
`_evaluate` with an oracle or a task-answer shortcut.

They are not, however, a proof of `do_algebra` on the prompt's intended input
domain. `spec.k` enumerates ten fixed operator-list shapes, with several
fixed operands, and contains no entry claim quantified over an arbitrary
contract-valid operator/operand list. Contract-valid examples such as two
additions, an exponentiation other than `2 ** 5`, most mixed expressions, and
all sufficiently long expressions satisfy no claim. That is a material
adequacy failure, not merely thin supporting evidence. The candidate therefore
does not contain the requested whole-program partial-correctness proof.

All candidate files were treated as untrusted. Candidate compiled artifacts,
caches, scripts, and claimed outputs were not used as proof evidence.

## 1. Input and provenance integrity

### Infrastructure and semantics-mode boundary

The trusted mount is consistent with `SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`:
`/reference/reference-semantics` exists. No infrastructure breach was found,
so a candidate verdict is appropriate.

The candidate's `reference-semantics/` is recursively identical to the trusted
tree:

- `diff -ru --no-dereference /reference/reference-semantics
  /candidate/reference-semantics` exited 0.
- The candidate semantics tree contains no symlink.
- No file is missing from, added to, mistyped in, or changed relative to the
  trusted semantics tree.

The candidate `prompt.py` and `py2mpy.py` are also byte-identical to their
trusted counterparts; both diffs exited 0 and the hashes agree. The complete
type manifest, commands, statuses, and hashes are in
[01_integrity.log](evidence/01_integrity.log), generated by
[01_integrity.sh](evidence/01_integrity.sh).

`verification.k`, `prompt.py`, `py2mpy.py`, and the supplied-semantics directory
are regular files/directories, not symlinks. The candidate also contains
untrusted extras (`prove.sh`, `smoke.mpy`, `kore-exec.tar.gz`, and a Python

do not substitute for the independent checks below.

## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks

### Natural-language contract

From trusted `/reference/prompt.py` and `/reference/canonical.py`, `do_algebra`
takes:

- at least one operator from `+`, `-`, `*`, `//`, `**`;
- at least two non-negative integer operands;
- exactly one more operand than operator;
- and returns the Python evaluation of the interleaved expression, including
  Python precedence, left associativity for `+`, `-`, `*`, `//`, and right
  associativity for `**`.

The prompt does not exclude a zero divisor. The canonical implementation raises
`ZeroDivisionError` for such an expression instead of returning an integer.
Accordingly, a normal-return theorem must either model that exceptional path or
state a sufficient nonzero-divisor precondition.

### Source algorithm

`solution.py` implements a precedence parser by recursive interval evaluation:

- level 0 scans from right to left for `+`/`-`, producing left associativity;
- level 1 scans from right to left for `*`/`//`;
- level 2 scans from left to right for `**`, producing right associativity;
- level 3 returns the selected operand.

This is a different algorithm from the canonical string construction plus
`eval`, which is acceptable if behavior agrees.

trusted canonical entry point and candidate entry point. It runs:

- the prompt example;
- minimum two-operand cases for all five operators;
- zero operands and `0 ** 0`;
- division by zero, comparing exception type and message;
- both scan directions and all associativity/precedence boundaries;
- the all-precedence expression;

  tokens, and operands 0 through 8. Generated cases contain at most one

